title: Universal algebraic complexity beyond generic corner cuts
objective: Prove a new structural theorem determining or substantially narrowing the worst-case asymptotic number of monomial initial ideals of finite polynomial algebras, starting with three variables and seeking a mechanism valid in every fixed dimension. Establish the strongest relevant primary baseline first. Success requires a complete uniform proof of sharp growth or a substantial asymptotic advance over that baseline for all colength-n ideals or all n-point configurations, a rigorous further algebraic, geometric or enumeration consequence, reproducible exact certificates and an honestly scoped manuscript. Examples, reformulations, already known corollaries and a plan alone do not complete this goal.
relationship_to_previous_goal: A new research objective. The completed corner-cut counting manuscript and its acceptance records remain separate and unchanged in mathematical content.
aspirational_endpoint: Determine the sharp asymptotic order of G_d(n) for every fixed dimension and explain quantitatively when algebraic dependencies increase the generic corner-cut count.

parameters.g_I: Number of distinct monomial initial ideals of I under global monomial orders.
parameters.G_d_n: Maximum g(I) over all fields K and ideals I in K[x_1,...,x_d] with dim_K(K[x]/I)=n.
parameters.F_d_n: Maximum g(I(P)) over all fields and n distinct K-rational points in d-dimensional affine space.
parameters.distinction: F_d(n) <= G_d(n). Do not transfer a point-ideal result to nonradical ideals without proof.
not_measured: Number of polynomials in one Groebner basis
Runtime of computing a basis without an explicit algorithm and input model

starting_bounds.generic: The existing manuscript proves C_d(n)=Theta_d(n^(d-1)(log n)^(d-1)).
starting_bounds.do_not_assume: G_d(n) has the same asymptotic order as C_d(n).

milestones.deliverable: A theorem-level primary-source comparison identifying the best relevant unrestricted and restricted bounds, exact hypotheses, input models and still viable targets.
A precise lemma about multiplication-compatible residue dependencies or state-polyhedron geometry, with its proof attempt and adversarial controls.
A symbolic realizable family and count proof, or a documented obstruction to the tested construction; finite examples alone are insufficient.
Sharp growth or a substantial advance over the strongest checked asymptotic bound for G_3 or all-point F_3, with explicit scope and a route to general fixed dimension where justified.
A proved algebraic, geometric or enumeration consequence beyond restating the count; any speed claim needs a full algorithmic complexity argument.
Complete proof, precise prior-art assessment, independently checked exact certificates and a separate honest manuscript suitable for the user's later review.

passes: Attempt a uniform dependency-sensitive upper-bound lemma
Attempt an infinite asymptotically stronger lower-bound family
required_controls: Onn--Sturmfels: C_2(7)=8<F_2(7)=10; the generic fan is not a universal refinement.
Grid complements preserve the Groebner fan and cannot amplify the basis count.
Every quotient model must satisfy commutation, cyclicity and the claimed length; arbitrary matroid data are insufficient.
Finite-field and characteristic-zero claims require their own hypotheses and cannot be interchanged.
initial_feasibility_gate.after_passes: Record a viable uniform mechanism, an existing theorem settling the target, or a precise remaining obstruction. An inconclusive report prompts a reasoned redirect and does not complete the theorem goal.
initial_feasibility_gate.search_expansion_rule: Increase n, characteristic or dimension only to test an explicit conjecture or discriminate between stated mechanisms.

acceptance_criteria: A theorem for a broad class, not only isolated configurations or a bounded enumeration.
Sharp asymptotics or a substantial improvement over the strongest relevant primary bound established by the first milestone.
A reusable structural proof explaining the effect of algebraic dependencies.
A rigorously established further consequence with its mathematical and algorithmic scope separated.
Exact reproducible certificates supporting, rather than replacing, a uniform proof.
An honest comparison and manuscript; impact, independent verification and journal acceptance are not presumed.

first_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, First feasibility pass: two rigorous route obstructions
first_feasibility_results.volume_obstruction: For n=binom(r+d,d), the generic state-moment polytope contains a simplex of volume A^(d-1)(A-dB)/d!, A=n(n-1)/2, B=nr/(d+1). This has order n^(2d); the whole-volume exponent cannot be reduced universally.
first_feasibility_results.lower_family_obstruction: For every three-variable quotient obtained by disjoint nontrivial socle relations in an N-point monomial order ideal, g(I)=O(n^(4/3)), n=length(I). This cannot exceed the existing generic order.
scope_exclusions: Relations with nonzero multiples in the quotient
first_feasibility_results.decision: Discard only the full-volume shrinking route and disjoint socle amplification route. Continue the primary-bound audit and investigate interacting multiplication-compatible dependencies.

second_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Second feasibility pass: interacting relations and a conditional count

all_socle_relation_spaces.hypotheses: I=J_D+R with D a finite monomial order ideal and R any linear relation space supported on its maximal monomials, in any field.
all_socle_relation_spaces.proof: Parallel downward chains from the maximal antichain are disjoint, so each total socle-coordinate sum is at most N-m <= n. Translating away the fixed standard monomials places the variable moment polytope in [0,n]^d. Apply the established lattice-polytope vertex theorem.
all_socle_relation_spaces.decision: Even arbitrary overlap confined to the socle cannot beat the generic order. Relations with surviving nonconstant multiples are required.

conditional_count.hypothesis: For an integer kappa>=1, every monomial box of volume at least kappa*n has quotient residues spanning the length-n algebra.
conditional_count.lemma: The first M=d^d*kappa*n monomials of every generic positive geometric order span the quotient. Greedy independence recovers its standard basis.
conditional_count.further_consequence: For fixed d and kappa, the minimum cardinality of a universal monomial-order list for this whole class is Theta_d,kappa(n^(d-1)(log n)^(d-1)), with the lower bound supplied by one generic point ideal.
conditional_count.scope: A conditional theorem, not an unrestricted bound or a new runtime theorem.
conditional_count.non_generic_control: The published seven-point F_29 configuration with ten initial staircases satisfies the rectangular condition with kappa=1, despite the generic count eight.

unrestricted_obstructions: For n diagonal points, kappa grows as Theta_d(n^(d-1)) even though g(I)=d for n>=2.

Translated Cartesian axis staircases give radical point ideals with g(I)=1, no identically zero monomial evaluations, and minimum representing-word/rank-completion length Omega_d(n^d). A uniform linear representative-word bound is false even for point ideals.
second_feasibility_results.completion_decision: Keep the full goal active. These supporting results identify the remaining mechanism and do not satisfy the all-ideal or all-point-configuration acceptance criterion.

third_feasibility_results.record: docs/interleaving_research.md, Third feasibility pass: binomial quotients and the boundary of the method

binomial_count.hypotheses: Any colength-n binomial ideal over any field in fixed dimension d>=2; monomial generators and nonradical quotients allowed.
binomial_count.conclusion: g(I)=O_d(n^(d-1)(log(n+1))^((d-1)^2)); in three variables O(n^2 log^4(n+1)).
binomial_count.proof: Known binomial normal forms give a partition residue matroid on the known hyperbolic cross V_n. Its moment polytope is the Minkowski sum of the n class hulls. Apply the published O_d(M^(d-1)) vertex bound with M<=|V_n|=O_d(n log^(d-1)n).
binomial_count.priority: Recorded as a consequence of existing tools; no novelty established.
binomial_count.scope: Not an unrestricted improvement, not a sharpness assertion, and not a new enumeration-runtime theorem.

failure_of_automatic_point_extension.circuit: -24+50*x-35*y+10*z-y^2=0; all five monomials lie in V_4^3, every four are independent.
failure_of_automatic_point_extension.conclusion: Five distinct nonzero residue lines have rank four; selecting class representatives independently fails already for a small radical point ideal.
failure_of_automatic_point_extension.limitation: Refutes the automatic partition-matroid extension, not all possible Minkowski decompositions.

finite_controls.models: K[t]/(t^n) and K[t]/(t^n-1), n=4,5,6,7,9, using actual commuting cyclic multiplication matrices.

third_feasibility_results.decision: Retain this positive comparison with surviving multiples, but do not start a separate binomial framework or paper. Continue toward a uniform mechanism for overlapping multi-term circuits under commuting multiplication.

truncated_partition_point_model.family: Distinct positive samples (t_j^A_1,...,t_j^A_d), with A_1=1 and integer positive exponents.
truncated_partition_point_model.uniform_rank_rule: The monomial residue rank is min(n, number of distinct A-degrees); proof by the positive-root bound for sparse polynomials, via Rolle induction.
truncated_partition_point_model.structure: Rank-n truncation of the degree-class partition matroid; genuine circuits of n+1 distinct classes.
truncated_partition_point_model.finite_control: For n=7, A=(1,6,9), t_j=j over Q, 37 initial staircases versus 36 generic corner cuts; all 86 staircases checked, with independent rational Gaussian checks of every positive witness.
truncated_partition_point_model.priority: A finite test of a mechanism, not a new asymptotic theorem or a claim of novelty.
truncated_partition_point_model.next_gate: Prove a symbolic count or a uniform obstruction for this family before enlarging enumeration.
